sources_considered.why: Primary lab document with 2025 hallucination rates for frontier models.
OpenAI research paper (Sept 2025) saying hallucinations persist in state-of-the-art systems.
A documented, consequential 2025 incident of hallucinated citations in a government report.
Reports OpenAI's claimed hallucination reductions for GPT-5 (counterevidence).

receipt.public_excerpt: More research is needed to understand the cause of these results.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's April 2025 frontier reasoning models hallucinated on 33% (o3) and 48% (o4-mini) of PersonQA questions, more than o1. OpenAI said it did not know why.

receipt.public_excerpt:
Such
“hallucinations” persist even in state-of-the-art systems and undermine trust.

evidence_items.explanation: In September 2025, OpenAI's own researchers wrote that hallucinations persist even in state-of-the-art systems and undermine trust.

receipt.public_excerpt: Deloitte has agreed to refund part of an Australian government contract after admitting it used generative AI to produce a report riddled with fake citations, phantom footnotes, and even a made-up quote from a Federal Court judgment.

evidence_items.explanation: A late-2025 real-world incident in which fabricated citations from a GPT-4o-based tool led to a partial refund on a government contract.

receipt.public_excerpt: GPT-5's responses are around 45 percent less likely to contain a factual error than GPT-4o and when thinking GPT-5's responses are around 80 percent less likely to contain a factual error than OpenAI o3

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI reported large relative cuts in factual errors with GPT-5. This shows real progress. It does not show that the problem went away, and the same article calls hallucination 'a major problem'.

unresolved_gaps: No single independent, cross-lab measure of hallucination rates at the end of 2025 was cited.
How much of a problem counts as 'haunting' is a judgment call.
